speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the emergency department. I understand you are presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after your birth. To begin my assessment, please tell me if your mother had any infections or fever during pregnancy or labor, and were you delivered via vaginal birth or cesarean section?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with secondary seizures due to perinatal asphyxia, likely exacerbated by antenatal chorioamnionitis and extremely low birth weight.
